title: In Joshua 18 What Does The Process Of Casting Lots Teach Us About Gods Guidance In Decision Making
paragraphs: The Significance of Casting Lots in Joshua 18: Insights into God’s Guidance

In Joshua 18, Israel finds itself at a pivotal moment. After years of conquest, the land of Canaan lies before them, ready to be distributed among the remaining seven tribes. The method God instructs Joshua to use for this division—casting lots—offers profound lessons about trusting in God’s sovereignty and guidance in our own decision-making.
Understanding Casting Lots: What Happened in Joshua 18?

After the conquest, Joshua gathers the Israelites at Shiloh and sets up the tent of meeting. Seven tribes have not yet received their inheritance, so Joshua instructs them to survey the land and write a description of it. Then, he says:
And ye shall describe the land into seven portions, and bring the description hither to me; and I will cast lots for you here before Jehovah our God. - Joshua 18:6 ASV

Casting lots was a common biblical practice for making decisions, especially when human wisdom alone could not determine the outcome. The process was not random chance but was seen as a means by which God’s will was revealed. Proverbs echoes this:
The lot is cast into the lap; But the whole disposing thereof is of Jehovah. - Proverbs 16:33 ASV
What Does This Teach Us About God’s Guidance?
Several key insights emerge from this episode in Joshua 18:

God Invites Us to Participate: Joshua instructs the tribes to survey and describe the land. This demonstrates that God values our involvement and preparation in the decision-making process. We are called to use the resources, wisdom, and discernment He gives us.

Ultimate Guidance Is God’s Prerogative: Even after careful preparation, the final decision comes from God. The Israelites submit their descriptions, but it is God who determines each tribe’s inheritance through the casting of lots. This reminds us that while planning is important, we must ultimately submit our plans to God, trusting Him for the outcome.

God’s Will Is Just and Impartial: By casting lots, every tribe had an equal opportunity. This method protected against favoritism or human manipulation, ensuring the distribution was fair and divinely appointed. God’s guidance is always just and trustworthy.

Faith in God’s Sovereignty: The Israelites accepted the results of the lots as God’s will. This required faith, humility, and a willingness to obey, even if the outcome differed from personal preferences. Similarly, we are called to trust God’s wisdom above our own.
Application for Today: How Do We Seek God’s Guidance?
While casting lots is not a normative practice for Christians today, the principles underlying it remain relevant:

Seek God in Prayer: We are encouraged to seek God’s will through prayer, asking for wisdom and discernment. But if any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him. - James 1:5 ASV
Depend on Scripture: God’s Word is the ultimate guide for our decisions. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and light unto my path. - Psalm 119:105 ASV

Yield to God’s Will: We must be ready to accept God’s direction, even if it differs from our own desires. Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding: In all thy ways acknowledge him, And he will direct thy paths. - Proverbs 3:5-6 ASV
Conclusion

The casting of lots in Joshua 18 teaches us to trust God’s sovereignty in every decision. While we are to use wisdom and participate actively in the process, our ultimate confidence must rest in God’s perfect will and guidance. As followers of Christ, we are called to seek Him first, trust His Word, and walk in faith—knowing that, just as He guided Israel, so He continues to guide His people today.
